$comment: PROPOSAL — NOT canonical, NOT vendored into the suite, NOT SHA-pinned, NOT adopted. Wire-contract draft for SHOW events: a podcast/scheduled show a user follows in radio-scan, published so others can discover and follow it. The feed-shaped sibling of station.v1 (a stream you tune) — see 'whyNotStation' below for the incident that forced the split. Lives in the external repo github.com/macos-node/radio-scan for TESTING ONLY. Kinds are locked provisionally against the suite's used set (1063/4550/27235/30000/31237/31238/31239 + radio-scan's 31240 airplay.v1 / 31241 station.v1): show.v1 = 31242, the next free slot, contiguous with the block. No .sha256 pin and no freeze governance apply until this is proposed to merge into the suite (ndisc/schema). Settles open decision #10 in docs/radio-scan-v0.2.0-direction-2026-08-10.md.
canonicalHome: macos-node/radio-scan — schema/show.v1.json (proposal; not yet in ndisc/schema)

authority.model: per-publisher key — any pubkey publishes its OWN followed-shows set; there is no single owner or gate. Identical to station.v1's model.
authority.note: Cross-user 'who else follows this show' filters on the feed URL via #r, and — when the feed carries a podcast:guid — on the stable #i identity. Prefer #i: it survives a feed moving host.

show.class: addressable — re-publishing the same d-tag replaces in place (edit metadata, no event spam)
show.kindRationale: A followed show is the same shape of record as a followed station — small, editable, per-user — so it takes the same addressable form. 31242 is the next free slot after station.v1's 31241 and is unused across the suite.
show.content: Optional human description of the show (plain text). The feed's own description is harvest, not wire — publish a note only if the user wrote one.
show.writtenBy: ntune (radio-scan's L4 UI), signed with the owner nsec from the OS keyring — the same key as ndisc/ntree/nsmpl (one person = one npub).

d.note: Addressable identity within the author. <slug> is a stable, filesystem-safe show name, derived from the feed title (same slugify as station.v1).

name.note: Human display name of the show.

r.note: The RSS/Atom FEED URL — not an episode enclosure, and not a stream mount. Single-letter tag so it is RELAY-FILTERABLE (#r), the same cross-user role it plays in station.v1. Note a feed URL is NOT a stable identity: measured 2026-08-18, feed.podbean.com/<show>/feed.xml and <show>.podbean.com/feed.xml served the byte-identical 4,053,739-byte document, and a URL-keyed dedupe treated them as two shows. Publish the URL the user subscribed with; use `i` for identity.

i.note: NIP-73 external content id carrying the feed's <podcast:guid> — the Podcasting-2.0 namespace GUID, stable across host moves and shared with non-Nostr podcast tooling. Single-letter, so #i is relay-filterable and is the PREFERRED cross-user key when present. Optional because plenty of feeds still omit it: of six live subscriptions sampled 2026-08-18, four carried one (podhome, yellowball, fountain.fm, nashownotes) and two did not (the BBC's, and podbean's — the very show that motivated this contract).

t.note: Genre / topic slug(s), lowercased (#t filterable). Align with the suite's genre slugs where they fit; free tags otherwise. ACCEPTED BUT NOT YET EMITTED by ntune: shows have no topic control (stations get theirs from the Add-station dialog), and the two candidate sources are both wrong to publish unasked — the feed's own categories are harvest, which this contract keeps off the wire, and the user's categories are typed into a private notes dialog and must not reach a relay by surprise. A deliberate topic control is the way in; until then the fixtures carry no `t` so they describe what is actually published.

alt.note: NIP-31 human-readable fallback for generic clients.

show.rule: Consumers MUST require only d + name + r structurally; every other tag (i/t/alt) is optional. A show with no descriptive tags is still valid — it is a bare 'I follow this feed' record.
show.harvestIsNotWire: The Tier-A identity ntune harvests from a feed (author, categories, language, copyright, website, owner email, funding, value) stays LOCAL — it is the feed's to state and any consumer can fetch it. The event publishes the follow, not a copy of the feed's metadata.

deletion.rule: An unfollow MUST tag BOTH the addressable `a` coordinate AND the concrete `e` event id.
deletion.why: Measured 2026-08-18: relay.fizx.uk accepted a-only deletions and went on serving every tombstoned station (7 of 7), while nos.lol and relay.primal.net honoured them — several implementations delete by event id only. Clients that filter deletions themselves are unaffected; anything trusting the relay is not.

whyNotStation.incident: 2026-08-10, two podcast feeds were published as station.v1 (airplay:station:on-the-wire — a blogspot RSS with ZERO audio enclosures — and airplay:station:a-duck-in-a-tree). They were removed locally but the relay copies survived until kind:5 deletions were issued 2026-08-18.
whyNotStation.reason: station.v1 defines `r` as 'the direct stream URL (the mount)' and #r as the cross-user identity of a TUNABLE stream. A feed URL there publishes a non-tunable row into that shared discovery space: any client filtering #r for a station gets something it cannot play. The two kinds keep #r honest per-kind.
whyNotStation.guardrail: ntune's publish_station now probes the URL and refuses a conclusively non-audio content-type, so the mistake cannot reach a relay again. That is a guard, not a home — this contract is the home.
whyNotStation.rootCause: Podcast follows had no wire form at all, so 'follow this stream' was the only publish button in the app.

ownShows.note: Rebuild the user's own followed-show set from the relays (relay = truth, local = cache) — exactly how ntune already reads its stations.

showFollowersByGuid.note: Cross-user discovery, PREFERRED: everyone who follows this show, however they reached its feed.

showFollowersByUrl.note: Cross-user discovery fallback for feeds with no podcast:guid. URL-keyed, so it misses followers who subscribed via a different hostname for the same feed.

relatedContracts.station.v1: schema/station.v1.json — the streaming sibling (kind 31241). Same author model, same addressable shape; `r` is a stream mount there and a feed URL here.
relatedContracts.airplay.v1: schema/airplay.v1.json — an observation of something heard. A future episode observation can reference its show by #i / #r or by this event's addressable `a` coordinate, exactly as it references a station today.
relatedContracts.nip73: External Content IDs — the source of the `i` tag format (podcast:guid:<guid>). Chosen over a bespoke tag so the identity is shared with non-Nostr podcast tooling.
relatedContracts.nip51-sets: A curated shared show list can reuse the suite's kind:30000 pattern. NIP-51 collection AUTHORING is open decision #9 and stays deferred — a show.v1 follow is the read-side half and does not cross that boundary.

changePolicy: PROPOSAL — free to edit; no SHA pin, no coordinated-wave governance yet. If/when proposed to merge into the suite, it adopts the suite discipline (SHA-pin at the authority, additive-only after freeze, kind confirmed unused, coordinated re-vendor across consumers) — see clip.v1.json for the model.
